sections.html:
Lafayette is a home rule city in southeastern Boulder County, between Boulder and Denver. It borders Erie to the north and east, Broomfield to the east and south, and Louisville to the southwest.

The city covers roughly 9.4 square miles at an elevation of 5,266 feet, and it had 30,411 residents at the 2020 census. US 287 is the main road through town, running north toward Longmont and south toward Broomfield and Denver. State Highway 7 leads east to Brighton and west to Boulder, and exit 229 off Interstate 25 gives access to the city. The NW Parkway is also listed among its highways.

Because the city touches Broomfield and Erie, a house with a Lafayette mailing address can sit in a different jurisdiction than you expect. Check the address against city limits before you assume which rules apply.

sections.h2: How did Lafayette begin, and why does coal still matter?
sections.html:
Lafayette was founded in 1888 by Mary E. Miller, who platted the town on part of the farm she and her husband Lafayette Miller had bought in 1868. Coal was discovered on the Miller farm in 1884, and the first Simpson Mine shaft was sunk in 1887.

The town became part of the Northern Coal Field boom that supplied Denver's households, smelters and power plants. Lafayette's last mine, the Black Diamond at today's US 287 and Baseline Road, closed in 1956, and the city shifted back to farming before suburban growth took over. Very little of the mining past remains, though a few structures moved from the mine camps still stand in Old Town.

In Old Town, newer townhomes stand beside the historic commercial buildings on Simpson Street. A house near the original 1888 plat may be decades older than one in a newer subdivision, and the repair questions a buyer asks will differ accordingly.

Lafayette is a small city, and its census numbers show a compact housing market. The table below collects figures from the 2020 census as summarized for the city.

MeasureValue
Population, 2020 census30,411
Households, 202012,070
Housing units, 202012,456
Vacant units3.1%
Median age38.9 years
Elevation5,266 feet

Only 3.1 percent of housing units were vacant in 2020, and the homeowner vacancy rate was 0.4 percent. Very few empty homes means sellers here are not competing with a large pool of vacant listings, though a house that needs work still has to be priced for its condition.

Lafayette's public schools belong to the Boulder Valley School District. Centaurus High School is the main public high school, and Angevine Middle School feeds into it.

  • Elementary schools: Lafayette Elementary, Alicia Sanchez, Bernard D. 'Pat' Ryan STEAM School and Pioneer Elementary, a bilingual English and Spanish school.
  • Peak to Peak Charter School serves kindergarten through high school.
  • Alexander Dawson School is a private K-12 school in the north part of town.

Families moving into the area often start with school boundaries, so a seller who can point to the district and the named schools saves a buyer a research step. Boundaries change, so confirm assignments with the district rather than a listing.

sections.h2: What is there to do in Lafayette, and who lives here?
sections.html:
The city's most popular recreation spot is Waneka Lake Park, which covers 147 acres with a 1.2 mile trail, fishing areas, playgrounds and picnic shelters. The park also holds the Waneka Granary, built in the 1870s and described as the city's oldest structure.

Old Town centers on Public Road and Chester Street, where Festival Plaza hosts community events. Lafayette also holds a peach festival, a wine festival and Lafayette Days each year.

Lafayette's central spot between Boulder, Longmont and Broomfield means a house here can draw interest from several directions. A house that sits unfinished through repairs, though, still costs its owner taxes, utilities and insurance every month.

sections.h2: When are Lafayette property taxes due?
sections.html:
Lafayette homeowners pay property tax to the Boulder County Treasurer, and the 2026 schedule offers two half payments or one full payment. In Colorado you can pay all at once or in two equal installments.

Option2026 due date (Boulder County)
First halfMarch 2
Second halfJune 15
Full paymentApril 30

The county gives no discount for early payment. A first-half payment made in March carries 1 percent interest and climbs to 6 percent by August. For taxes due that year, the postmark date on a mailed payment counts as the payment date. Checks go to the Boulder County Treasurer, and cash should never be mailed.

The Treasurer's office is in Boulder at 1325 Pearl Street, and the county's Lafayette location at 1755 S. Public Road is listed as closed until late January 2027. Full details are on the Boulder County due dates page.

If you sell during the year, the closing company prorates the bill between you and the buyer, so ask your title officer how it will be handled before you sign.

sections.h2: How does selling a Lafayette house work with a cash buyer?
sections.html:
Selling to a cash buyer in Lafayette removes the loan and appraisal steps, so the closing date depends mostly on the title work and your schedule. The deed is recorded through the Boulder County Clerk and Recorder, and a title company handles the transfer.

  • You tell us about the house, its condition and any tenants.
  • We review the property and make an offer, or tell you plainly why we cannot.
  • If you accept, the title company prepares closing documents and the tax proration.
  • You pick a closing date that fits your move.

We buy houses as they are, so you do not need to paint, replace flooring or clear the garage. An as-is sale suits inherited houses, houses with tenants and houses where a repair estimate is more than the owner wants to spend.

Lafayette grew from 8,985 people in 1980 to 30,411 in 2020, and most of that growth came after the coal era ended. The census counts below show the pattern.

Census yearPopulation
19808,985
199014,548
200023,197
201024,453
202030,411

The city is governed by a seven member council elected on a nonpartisan basis in odd-numbered years, with a city administrator running daily operations. Lafayette also formed its first sister city partnership in 2025, with Iquitos in Peru.

Growth on that scale means many houses in town were built in different decades, across a long span of years. A buyer who works with cash can look at any of them in their present condition.

sections.h2: What do Lafayette sellers usually run into?
sections.html:
Lafayette sellers most often cite timing, condition and carrying costs. Each is easier to manage once you know your options.

  • A job change that moves you out of the Boulder and Denver corridor.
  • An older Old Town house with updates you cannot afford.
  • A property inherited from a relative who lived in Lafayette for decades.
  • A rental you no longer want to manage.

If one of these describes your situation, send us the address. There is no cost to ask, and you decide whether to move forward.

faqs.q: What county is Lafayette, CO in?
faqs.a: Lafayette is in southeastern Boulder County. Property tax is billed by the Boulder County Treasurer and deeds are recorded with the Boulder County Clerk and Recorder.

faqs.q: When are 2026 property taxes due in Lafayette?
faqs.a: Boulder County lists March 2 and June 15 for two half payments, or April 30 for a single full payment. There is no discount for paying early.

The Boulder Valley School District serves Lafayette. Centaurus High School and Angevine Middle School are the main public secondary schools, and Peak to Peak Charter School offers kindergarten through high school.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lafayette house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases the house as it stands, so you do not have to repair, paint or clean before closing. We will factor the condition into the offer.
The city had 30,411 residents at the 2020 census and covers about 9.4 square miles. It borders Erie, Broomfield and Louisville.
